title: JWT Bearer Authentication
description: JWT Bearer authentication lets your API validate access tokens without cookies. It is the standard way to secure stateless APIs in modern .NET applications.

data.text: JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are compact, URL-safe tokens that carry claims about a user. With JWT Bearer authentication, the client sends the token in the Authorization header, and your API validates it without hitting a database or session store.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install the JWT Bearer authentication handler.

data.title: Configuring JWT Bearer
data.content: Add JWT Bearer authentication in Program.cs.

terms.definition: A compact, signed token that contains claims and is transmitted in the Authorization header.
A token presented in the Authorization header as 'Bearer <token>'.
Settings that define how the JWT handler validates the issuer, audience, signature, and expiration.

data.title: Secret Management
data.text: Never hard-code signing keys. Use Azure Key Vault, environment variables, or user secrets in development.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: JWT Bearer auth is stateless and ideal for APIs
Tokens are validated using a signing key and metadata
data.takeaway: JWT Bearer authentication is the standard way to secure modern .NET APIs.

data.title: Exercise: Protect an API Endpoint
data.description: Require a valid JWT to access a weather forecast endpoint.
steps: Add JWT Bearer authentication with a known signing key
Generate a JWT using jwt.io or a small console utility
Call the endpoint without a token (expect 401), then with a valid token (expect 200)
data.expectedOutcome: Only requests with a valid JWT receive the weather data.
